author: ValWood
body:
In yeast

Yeast does not synthesize carnosine (because they lack β-alanine biosynthesis and carnosine synthase).

The CARNMT1 ortholog in yeast (MTC7) probably has other substrate specificities since yeast doesn’t appear to encounter it endogenously.

heterologous expression of mammalian CARNMT1 in yeast with supplied carnosine, the enzyme retained activity, showing the evolutionary conservation of function but under normal physiology, yeast’s MTC7 is probably acting on different histidine-containing metabolites.
title: RHEA mapping for yeast RHEA:14205

author: ValWood
body:
Here is a supporting refernece
https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.2215431120?utm_source=chatgpt.com
Lastly, evidence for the substrate specificity of YNL092W remains inconclusive. YNL092W catalyzes methylation of carosine in vitro, and this is in agreement with its mammalian homologs ([55](https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.2215431120?utm_source=chatgpt.com#core-collateral-r55)). However, yeast does not natively produce carosine, suggesting that this is not its bona fide activity.
